text:
Dear McDonald’s Surfers Paradise Team,

I am writing to formally raise a serious concern following my visit to your restaurant yesterday.

While waiting for my lunch order, I witnessed a staff member — visible from the front counter — coughing repeatedly while handling food in the kitchen area.

Disturbed by this, I asked the manager whether this particular individual would be preparing my meal. I was reassured that he would not be.

However, despite this assurance, I saw the same person — the one who had been coughing — preparing what appeared to be my burger.

I felt extremely uncomfortable and unable to eat the meal as I had just witnessed him coughing without any attempt to shield his mouth or follow proper hygiene protocols.

I returned to the counter and requested a refund, explaining that I could not eat the food prepared by someone visibly unwell.

The staff member I spoke with apologised and claimed that the individual was actually the cleaner.

Regardless of their title, this person was clearly involved in food preparation.

To make matters worse, I overheard the manager shout, “Hey Nathan, you should be wearing a mask,” to which the individual responded with laughter and continued working — still coughing.

As a customer, I find this completely unacceptable. McDonald’s is a global brand known for upholding strict health and safety standards.

It is deeply concerning to see basic food safety practices so blatantly disregarded.

McDonald’s prides itself on the quality and safety of its food — but that commitment is undermined when sick staff are allowed to handle meals.

I trust this incident will be taken seriously, and I would appreciate a response outlining the steps being taken to ensure this does not happen again.
author: Nicky Grady

text:
On New Year’s Eve, I was treated extremely unprofessionally by two of the female staff members working. They were screaming and swearing at a group of more than 20 people, which was completely unacceptable. In over 30 years, I have never been treated like this by any business.

I understand that customer-facing roles can be stressful and that everyone deserves an opportunity to work, but this behaviour was far beyond what is acceptable. No business can operate successfully with staff showing this kind of attitude toward customers.

Unfortunately, the situation was also poorly handled by management. The manager on duty did not address the issue in a professional manner at all. If further clarification is needed, the business can review their security camera footage from around 12:05 am, which clearly shows the behaviour and language used by the staff. Some employees were also on their phones during this time.

I have photos and videos of the incident and am happy to provide them if required.

Very disappointing experience, especially on New Year’s Eve.
